text:
aisha-partnerships: Kicking off onboarding for OpenFlux (new model provider). Main goals: confirm redistribution/license terms, export-control posture, and checklist for cloud marketplace listing + hardware packaging. Quick sync notes here, please react with :thumbsup: when you've read.

mike-legal: Thanks — two red flags up front: 1) OpenFlux wants CC-BY style for model card but unclear on weights. 2) Their contributor agreement references a third-party dataset with unknown license. Need a short questionnaire.

sanjay-tech: For weights packaging: prefer we ask for both FP16 and int8 quantized artifacts. It'll make Dedicated/Docker builds easier. Also need a reproducible seed + model config.json.

elena-pm: Marketplace metadata we need: model name, version, size, FLOPs estimate, tags (e.g., llm, reranking), and a recommended SKU mapping for Hosted vs Dedicated. Can we standardize a 3-tier SKU suggestion?

joshua-ops: Ops note — if they want redistribution in a marketplace, we need S3 staging in our partner bucket + signed manifests. Also KMS key policy for customer test images. We should include that in onboarding doc.

mike-legal: I drafted a short export-control check we can run. Link: https://redwood.tools/internal/export-checklist (private). Key Qs: country of origin of training data, whether model uses controlled architectures, and whether authors know of embargoed contributors.

aisha-partnerships: @mike-legal can you paste the small clause we'd like to include in the distribution addendum? we need something one-paragraph for initial LOI.

mike-legal: Sure. Proposed clause (short):
```
"Provider warrants that it has the necessary rights to distribute the model weights and that no portion of the training data or model artifacts infringes third-party IP or violates export control laws. Provider agrees to complete Redwood's export-control questionnaire and to cooperate in remediation if any restricted content is identified."
```

sanjay-tech: From infra: please ask them to produce a minimal Dockerfile and a model validator script we can run: `python validate_model.py --weights path --config config.json`. That speeds onboarding by days.

elena-pm: Also for the marketplace listing: let's plan a joint announcement only after we complete an internal security scan + a canary run on Dedicated for 48h. Timelines? vendor asks for a co-announcement in 3 weeks. I think 4-6 weeks realistic.

joshua-ops: Agree 4-6 weeks. Ops can support a 48h canary starting week 3 if package/validator are clean. Need a toggle to disable telemetry during canary for privacy asks.

aisha-partnerships: I'll send OpenFlux the initial LOI + the export checklist and ask for artifacts (FP16, int8, config, Dockerfile, and validator). Also will propose a 4-week timeline and co-announcement in week 5 if all green.

vendor-bot: Checklist created: https://redwood.tools/internal/onboarding/openflux-checklist.md - includes: legal questionnaire, export-control form, tech artifacts list, marketplace metadata template, ops packaging steps.

mike-legal: One more: please request a short negative covenant re: downstream model redistribution to 3rd-party hosting (we're OK with marketplace, but not with unfettered rehosting). I'll draft language.

aisha-partnerships: Good. I'll add that to the LOI. Anything else?

sanjay-tech: If they claim any non-disclosure for certain dataset sources, flag to Research for a provenance review before canary.

elena-pm: Add a field in the marketplace template for "recommended latency/throughput targets" so we can pre-configure Dedicated instance types.

aisha-partnerships: Perfect. I'll compile and send to OpenFlux today. Thanks everyone — ping me in DM if blockers. :rocket:
